user-insights: Your app already knows what users want. It's in the events, the feedback and the requests. Read it together and you know what to build next, with the numbers to back it.
product-teardown: Every good product is a pile of decisions you can learn from. Study how one handles copy, onboarding and pricing, and walk away with moves that fit your own product.
decision-doc: Most stalled projects are a decision nobody wrote down. Pick one option, name the owner and what would reopen it, and the team stops arguing it again.
product-spec: Building goes fast when nobody has to guess. Turn the idea into scope, flows, data and acceptance criteria, and you ship the thing you meant.
agent-instructions: Agents work best when they know how your repo actually runs. Give them the real commands and rules, and they stop guessing and breaking the build.
supabase: Most Supabase bugs are access bugs. Get tables, policies and typed clients right from the start, and every user only ever sees their own data.
auth-implementation: Sign-in is the easy part. Making every route check who's asking is the hard part. Get both right and nobody reads data that isn't theirs.
interface-design: A good screen comes from the product's job, not a template. Design from the real content and every state, and people find what they came for.
ui-copy: Interface words are part of the product. Write them from what the code actually does, and users know what happens before they click.
ai-product-development: An AI feature is a product, not a prompt. Typed contracts, every UI state, evals and cost limits mean it holds up when real users hit it.
payments-with-dodo: Billing breaks quietly. Wire checkout, webhooks, entitlements and refunds end to end, and people get exactly what they paid for, every time.
credit-metering: Credits are money, so treat them like a ledger. Reserve, capture and refund cleanly, and usage stays fair even with retries and parallel requests.
rate-limit: Every public route is a bill waiting to happen. Limit by who's calling, decide what happens when Redis is down, and abuse stops costing you.
email-with-resend: Email is where trust is won or lost. Send with consent, suppression and retries handled, and the right message lands exactly once.
remove-ai-slop: Generic design makes a product forgettable. Find the patterns that read as AI-made, see each fix side by side, and your product looks like yours.
mobile-first: Most people meet your product on a phone. Fix what breaks between 320 and 768 pixels, measured before and after, and it works in their hand.
performance-diagnosis: Slow is a symptom, not a cause. Measure first, find the real bottleneck, and the page gets faster where users actually feel it.
search-ready: Good pages go unread when search can't understand them. Fix metadata, schema and crawl rules route by route, and people find you.
social-sharing: A shared link is a first impression. Get the titles, images and previews right on every route, and every share looks intentional.
readme: A README is the front door of a repo. Check that every command actually runs, and new people get from clone to working in minutes.
deploy-check: Most bad deploys were visible before the push. Check tests, secrets, migrations and rollback first, and you ship knowing it's safe.
changelog: Shipping counts for more when people can see it. Turn the git log into notes users understand, and every release earns attention.
skill-creator: Any workflow you repeat is a skill waiting to be written. Package it with tests, and your agent does it the same good way every time.
landing-copy: Visitors decide in seconds. Lead with one claim you can prove, and they understand why it matters to them before they scroll.
landing-page: A landing page has one job: help one visitor make one decision. Build it around that and real proof, and more of them say yes.
image-editing: Edited images drift away from the original. Track the references and check every revision, and the product still looks like itself.
demo-video: A demo is the fastest way to show what you built. Plan the beats, write the script, render the video, and people get it in a minute.
analytics: You can't improve what you don't measure. Define the events that matter, wire them correctly, and decisions start from real numbers.
product-launch: A launch is a plan, not a post. Pick the audience, the channels and the signup path, and launch day turns into actual users.
cold-outreach: Cold messages work when they're about the reader. Lead with a real reason to talk, keep the facts checkable, and more people reply.
humanize: Readers stop trusting text that sounds generated. Strip the AI patterns, keep the facts and the voice, and it reads like a person wrote it.
product-experiments: Most tests prove nothing because the rules come after the data. Set the decision rule first, and every result tells you what to do.
ai-cost-audit: AI costs hide inside every call. Price each action, user and plan from real usage, and you see what to cut without hurting quality.
fundraising: Investors fund a story the numbers back up. Tie every claim to evidence and get the round math right, and the pitch holds up under questions.
